t: Count Good Subarrays (OR Equals an Element)
o: A subarray is good if its bitwise OR equals one of its own elements. Since OR is at least every element, OR equals an element iff OR equals the MAXIMUM element. So we count subarrays where OR(l..r) == max(l..r). For [4,2,3] that is 4 subarrays; for [1,3,1] all 6 qualify.
k: OR(sub) >= max(sub) always, so good <=> OR == max.
For fixed r, both suffix-OR and suffix-max take at most ~30 distinct values as l varies; keep them as segment lists (value, leftmost index) updated in O(30) per step.
Merge-walk the two segment lists by left endpoint and add up lengths of overlaps where the values coincide.

a.i: Maintain, for the current r, the partition of l in [0..r] into maximal segments of constant suffix OR and constant suffix max. Adding nums[r] prepends a new segment and ORs/maxes the old values (collapsing equals). Both lists are sorted by left endpoint with monotone values, so a two-pointer sweep counts, for each l-range where the OR value equals the max value, the number of left endpoints.
s: For each r: rebuild the OR segment list (new value nums[r] at l=r, then OR previous values, skipping duplicates); same for max.
Two-pointer over both lists: for the overlapping l-range of the current pair of segments, if values are equal add the range length.
Advance the pointer whose segment ends first.
a.t: O(30 n) — each step rebuilds two segment lists of length <= 31 and merges them

w: Reducing 'OR equals some element' to 'OR equals max' is the key insight; then the classic 'at most 30 distinct suffix ORs' technique finishes it. A brute force over all O(n^2) subarrays with incremental OR is O(n^2) and too slow at 1e5. Pitfalls: zeros (a subarray of zeros is good since OR = 0 = max), and off-by-one in segment boundaries. Follow-up: count subarrays where OR equals the minimum, or where OR is divisible by k.
